title: April client exploration

candidates.name: Swift / AppKit + WKWebView
candidates.basis: macOS adapter and optional shell candidate; a Swift-only shared core is no longer the direction.
candidates.strength: Direct platform APIs and familiar macOS interaction; web engine for rich documents.
candidates.risk: Platform-specific UI; shared core adds bridging and packaging work.
candidates.next: Build one native panel, a long wiki and an AX observer; compare effort with Tauri.

candidates.name: Tauri + Rust core
candidates.basis: Explore as a shared desktop UI around a platform-agnostic core; framework remains undecided.
candidates.strength: Web content flexibility with a native core and system webviews.
candidates.risk: macOS integrations need native code; webview differences and IPC require testing.
candidates.next: Implement the same wiki, voice controls and AX operation as the Swift slice.

candidates.name: GPUI
candidates.basis: Conditional candidate for an editor-like workspace.
candidates.strength: GPU-rendered custom workspace; real editor use through Zed.
candidates.risk: Document, accessibility and platform behavior need validation; tied to Zed development.
candidates.next: Test long selectable text, input methods, VoiceOver and native overlay integration.

candidates.name: Wails
candidates.basis: Alternative if Go is preferred; no language preference confirmed.
candidates.strength: Go services plus flexible web documents using OS webview.
candidates.risk: Deep macOS integration still needs bridging; evaluate native audio integration.
candidates.next: Compare developer effort and lifecycle behavior with the Tauri slice.

candidates.name: Raven
candidates.basis: Assistant recommendation to deprioritize; user has not ruled it out.
candidates.strength: Small C core; XML designer, editor widgets, GPU rendering and multiple bindings.
candidates.risk: Changing 0.2 API; document depth and accessibility need independent validation.
candidates.next: Revisit after a representative document and accessibility prototype succeeds.

candidates.name: Iced
candidates.basis: Mentioned and positioned; no detailed evaluation performed.
candidates.strength: Cross-platform Rust GUI focused on simplicity and type safety.
candidates.risk: Document-heavy product fit and native integrations remain untested.
candidates.next: Revisit if Rust-only UI becomes a requirement.

candidates.name: Slint
candidates.basis: Mentioned; no detailed product-fit or licensing evaluation performed.
candidates.strength: Declarative custom interfaces; AccessKit integration is documented.
candidates.risk: Rich document workflow, licensing fit and platform details need review.
candidates.next: Validate document editing requirements before investing in a prototype.

candidates.name: egui / Dear ImGui
candidates.basis: Recommended for inspectors rather than primary document workspace.
candidates.strength: Immediate-mode tools, debugging and application inspectors.
candidates.risk: Wiki and rich application UX would require more product-specific work.
candidates.next: Consider as an embedded diagnostics surface.

candidates.name: Fyne
candidates.strength: Cross-platform Go UI without a web runtime.
candidates.risk: Rich editable documents and deep macOS behavior remain untested.
candidates.next: Revisit if Go-only UI and simpler content become priorities.

candidates.name: Gio
candidates.strength: Custom immediate-mode GPU UI with broad platform coverage.
candidates.risk: More document infrastructure expected than a webview approach.
candidates.next: Prototype text selection, IME and VoiceOver if reconsidered.

candidates.name: Qt / PySide
candidates.strength: Mature desktop controls and model/view architecture.
candidates.risk: Deployment, licensing fit and document/native UX should be weighed against macOS focus.
candidates.next: Revisit for complex traditional data views or an existing Qt team.

candidates.name: Flutter
candidates.basis: Broader cross-platform baseline; no mobile-first requirement.
candidates.strength: Shared custom UI across desktop, mobile and web.
candidates.risk: Native automation remains separate; document UX needs a representative test.
candidates.next: Revisit if mobile parity becomes an immediate requirement.

candidates.name: Avalonia / WPF-style UI
candidates.basis: Mentioned as an alternative; WPF itself is Windows-specific.
candidates.strength: Avalonia offers cross-platform XAML, binding and MVVM tooling.
candidates.risk: No .NET preference; macOS automation and document surfaces remain to be evaluated.
candidates.next: Revisit if a C# core or team makes it compelling.

candidates.name: Electron
candidates.basis: Reopened as a shared UI baseline after confirming cross-platform core direction; measure footprint rather than assuming.
candidates.strength: Consistent bundled Chromium and broad web UI ecosystem.
candidates.risk: Measure idle resource use and native module packaging against system webviews.
candidates.next: Compare the identical document/audio workload if webview compatibility becomes costly.

candidates.name: Obsidian as required vault host
candidates.basis: User chose a unified April app without app hopping. This is a confirmed product decision.
candidates.strength: Existing Markdown workspace, file navigation and tabs.
candidates.risk: Separate required host conflicts with the chosen unified experience; plugin permissions are not vault isolation.
candidates.next: Keep Obsidian as a UX reference; use reusable components inside April instead.
candidates.notes: DOCX preview is sufficient; full Word editing is not initially required.

experiments.title: Native accessibility spike
experiments.procedure: Read a window tree, subscribe to changes and perform one scoped action across several real apps. Exercise denied/revoked permission, stale elements and missing semantics.
experiments.evidence: Record coverage, failures and recovery; define screenshot/OCR fallback boundaries.

experiments.title: Rich document workload
experiments.procedure: Render and edit a representative long wiki with tables, links, code, citations and a streaming conversation. Exercise selection, search, IME, copying and scroll anchoring.
experiments.evidence: Measure UI stalls and memory with the same fixture in each candidate.

experiments.title: Interruptible voice under load
experiments.procedure: Run capture/playback while streaming text and scrolling the wiki; interrupt speech and switch audio devices.
experiments.evidence: Measure interruption-to-playback-stop time, dropouts and recovery; set targets before comparing.

experiments.title: Accessible agent interface
experiments.procedure: Navigate shell, document and conversation with keyboard and VoiceOver, including focus changes and streaming announcements.
experiments.evidence: Verify names, roles, reading order, text navigation and non-disruptive updates.

experiments.title: macOS lifecycle and distribution
experiments.procedure: Test menu bar, overlay focus, multiple windows, sleep/wake, permission prompts and signed application behavior.
experiments.evidence: Record packaging effort and behavior on supported macOS versions.

experiments.title: Cloud coordinator boundary
experiments.procedure: Connect a local interaction to a mock specialist task with reconnect, cancellation, retry and result provenance.
experiments.evidence: Verify duplicate suppression and that local permissions are not implicitly granted to cloud jobs.

experiments.title: Self-extension review slice
experiments.procedure: Conversation → scoped feature → implementation/test → dev preview → PR and artifacts → user review → approved release. Discuss substantial scope before implementation.
experiments.evidence: Demonstrate approval associated with reviewed scope and candidate; define rollback.

experiments.title: Offline queue and reconnection
experiments.procedure: Disconnect, submit typed request, show pending state, reconnect and reconcile. No offline voice is promised.
experiments.evidence: No lost or duplicated requests; define edit/cancel and conflict behavior.

experiments.title: Mac activation, focus and display prototype
experiments.procedure: Held-key activation persists after release; double-press/voice dismisses. Test notch and non-notch displays, current-app focus and external active monitor.
experiments.evidence: No focus theft; visible listening/speaking states; verify device and failure behavior.

experiments.title: Unified vault and artifact slice
experiments.procedure: In April, browse Markdown, DOCX preview and isolated interactive content. Indicate new/edited/action-required items. Exercise cross-context accessible vault and expiring private grant.
experiments.evidence: No app hopping for core workflow; unread artifacts do not block tasks; private access expires without ordinary-memory retention.

decisions.title: Platform-agnostic core; macOS integration first
decisions.rationale: Confirmed by user: design the core for macOS, Linux and Windows. Implement accessibility and other native capabilities on macOS first; Windows and Linux adapters follow. This does not require simultaneous feature parity.

decisions.title: One interaction agent with specialists
decisions.rationale: Prior chat and wiki: coding, research/wiki, artifacts and recording specialists behind one relationship.

decisions.title: Cloudflare cloud platform
decisions.rationale: Prior chat preference. Specific services, current limits and implementation choices require revalidation.

decisions.title: GUI framework and document surface
decisions.rationale: Reassess shared UI options against a platform-agnostic core. Tauri, Electron, Wails and custom-rendered options remain candidates; no framework or language is selected.

decisions.title: Separate UI, automation and audio responsibilities
decisions.rationale: Use a shared core with platform adapters, starting on macOS. Specific interfaces, audio execution model and process boundaries remain proposed until validated.

decisions.title: Final GUI framework and core language
decisions.rationale: No final framework or language has been selected. No candidate is user-confirmed as ruled out.

decisions.title: Voice-first surfaces
decisions.rationale: Voice is primary, activated by a button or wake word; exact activation defaults remain open. Chat is secondary. Surface background results as artifacts, websites and interactive interfaces for input and action.

decisions.title: Client rollout
decisions.rationale: Mac alone first, then web, then native Android. Core remains portable across macOS, Windows and Linux; later desktop and iOS timing is open.

decisions.title: Context-aware notifications
decisions.rationale: Choose delivery using priority, need for user action, active device and work/social context exposed by devices. Signal sources, permissions and interruption thresholds remain open; continuous surveillance is not implied.

decisions.title: Adjustable autonomy and learned approval
decisions.rationale: Start restrictive and ask more often early. User can tighten or relax guardrails. Explore an approver model learning from approvals and denials, approving suitable actions within delegated authority and flagging exceptions. Rule promotion and fixed boundaries remain open.

decisions.title: Queryable and parallel memory
decisions.rationale: Provide agent-queryable retrieval and a parallel model maintaining memory and enriching conversations. Store/use ordinary memory quietly, with inspection and controls over retention. Research Supermemory and alternatives later; no provider selected.

decisions.title: Sensitive memory exception
decisions.rationale: Keep financial and medical information separate from ordinary memory. Explicit user tagging or requests grant provisional access for a specific task. General retention and unrelated reuse are not authorized. Storage, expiry, revocation and derived-data cleanup remain open.

decisions.title: Self-extension bootstrap
decisions.rationale: Begin with conversation, add coding for April itself and development deployments, then grow capabilities incrementally. Initial flow: tested feature and dev preview, PR with artifacts, user review/approval, then merge and production. No deployment is being performed now.

decisions.title: User-led feature readiness
decisions.rationale: Discuss substantial features before implementation; April may arrange a discussion or user may initiate one. User decides when the plan is ready. Conversational PR reviews are desired over time; scheduling and approval-recording mechanics remain open.

decisions.title: Offline-first and eager sync
decisions.rationale: Cloud is the source of truth. Persist locally and sync eagerly when online. Initially offline typed chat queues requests; live voice is unavailable. Local inference is not required; reconnect dispatch, conflicts and offline artifact availability remain open.

decisions.title: Unified April application
decisions.rationale: Keep voice, vault browser, previews and interactive artifacts in one April application. Obsidian is a UX reference; a required separate Obsidian host is ruled out. Reuse libraries; GUI framework and core language remain open.

decisions.title: Mac voice activation and focus
decisions.rationale: Hold a configurable key to activate an ongoing voice session; release does not end it. Dismiss by spoken request or double-press. Preserve keyboard focus in the current app. Timing and failure behavior remain open.

decisions.title: Notch and multi-monitor presence
decisions.rationale: Listening and speaking have distinct wave/blob states. On notched displays emerge from the notch. On non-notched displays stay invisible until activated, then show a top-center indicator below the menu bar. Appear on the screen the user is actively working on, including external monitors.

decisions.title: User-owned multi-vault artifacts
decisions.rationale: Vaults are user-chosen storage folders with a default and additional vaults. Conversations do not belong to a vault; public-to-April vaults are available across conversations. Private access remains explicit and task scoped. Browsing a vault is not a session switch.

decisions.title: Private vault grants
decisions.rationale: Private-vault information requires explicit, specific, temporary access that expires. Financial/medical information remains excluded from ordinary memory. Grant duration, operations, revocation and derived-context cleanup remain open.

decisions.title: Non-blocking artifact browsing
decisions.rationale: Indicate new and edited artifacts in the vault browser. User can inspect now or later; unread items do not block subsequent work. Actual required user input or approval may block dependent work.

decisions.title: Artifact types and preview scope
decisions.rationale: Support Markdown, DOCX previews, JavaScript source and interactive artifacts within April. Full Word editing is not initially required. Interactive execution needs an isolated surface; library and rendering choices remain open.

decisions.title: Replaceable realtime voice provider
decisions.rationale: Start with OpenAI realtime voice, with natural spoken interruption and a replaceable provider layer preserving required behaviors. Review official capabilities before design; cross-provider feature equivalence is unproven. Wake-word investigation is deferred.

decisions.title: Initial coding scope and GitHub review
decisions.rationale: Start with April's own repositories only; the user adds other projects later. Host repositories on GitHub and use GitHub PRs and reviews as the review record, including when discussions happen through April. No repository creation, push or credential setup is requested by this design discussion.

decisions.title: Cloudflare specialist execution
decisions.rationale: Confirmed: agent coordination and coding builds/tests run on Cloudflare, following the existing specialist architecture. Mac supplies native interaction and device integrations. A platform-specific macOS build/signing/testing plan remains an engineering question, not a preference to reopen.

decisions.title: Cloud-hosted vault sync and access separation
decisions.rationale: Both public-to-April and private vaults live on Cloudflare and sync eagerly with local artifacts whenever connected. Cloudflare is authoritative; encryption and secure defaults are required. Sync does not grant agent use of private data. Key custody, encryption scheme, recovery and sync details remain open.

decisions.title: Centralized explicit approval flow
decisions.rationale: Every approval request routes through a central approval agent/service. It shows an overlay with the scope and records a user button click in an audit log. Private-vault approval cannot be inferred from speech; April cannot bypass the approval service. Mandatory private consent remains distinct from learned approvals within policy. Grant lifetime, revocation and enforcement implementation remain open.

decisions.title: Audience and distribution
decisions.rationale: Personal use first; later, anyone with a Cloudflare account and a MacBook should be able to use April. Initial multi-user service is not required.

decisions.title: Plugin architecture across integrations, specialists and artifacts
decisions.rationale: Confirmed major direction: plugin architecture for app/tool integrations (initially Cursor, Slack and browser), specialist subagents and vault artifact support (Markdown, PDFs, Word, interactive HTML and JavaScript). Detailed contracts, packaging, isolation, authority and lifecycle will be discussed later; no implementation chosen.

decisions.title: Staged desktop awareness and computer use
decisions.rationale: Initially see only content explicitly shared by the user. Later add broader desktop-app awareness and delegated interaction under the central permission model. Codex computer-use experience is the north star; deep dive deferred to a separate session. No initial ambient desktop monitoring or control.

decisions.title: English/Hindi voice and system audio
decisions.rationale: Initially English and Hindi, including primarily English conversations with occasional Hindi. Support microphone and system audio; music identification is an example task. Capture activation, permissions, retention and implementation remain open; continuous capture is not selected.

decisions.title: Background capture with visible listening indicator
decisions.rationale: Explicitly started listening/recording sessions continue when the workspace window closes, including meetings. Show a listening/capture indicator near the notch or equivalent whenever audio is captured. Inactive can stay invisible; active capture cannot. Closing workspace differs from dismissing the session. Retention, sleep behavior and start/stop details remain open; no automatic meeting recording is selected.

decisions.title: Reference transcription and opt-in audio retention
decisions.rationale: Reference transcription may lag. Do not retain audio by default after processing; user may explicitly request a saved recording for meetings/conversations as a backup. This supersedes earlier blanket no-audio remarks. Live voice responsiveness remains separate. Provider retention, temporary buffers and saved-recording expiry/deletion remain open.

decisions.title: Private access expires with the task
decisions.rationale: User confirms that private-vault access granted for a task stops when the task ends. It is not a continuing permission for later tasks. Terminal-state handling, early revocation and cached/derived-context cleanup remain implementation work.

decisions.title: Initial operating budget
decisions.rationale: Start with Cloudflare $5 base-plan expectation plus approximately $20/month AI; flexible AI budget based on use. Infrastructure fit is not verified. Overage behavior, warnings and caps remain open.

decisions.title: Evolving approval and conversational correction
decisions.rationale: Discover additional approval categories during use; existing mandatory consent remains. User asks April to correct noticed mistakes. Recoverable history is a recommendation, not yet selected; irreversible side effects need separate treatment.

decisions.title: Efficient, fluid client over shipping speed
decisions.rationale: Prioritize efficient resource use and fluid/non-janky interactions over shipping sooner. Evaluate idle CPU/memory/battery and under-load responsiveness. Numeric targets, minimum hardware and framework remain open.

decisions.title: Soft AI budget nudge
decisions.rationale: $20 monthly AI threshold is non-blocking. Ask/nudge about increased spend, but keep working while pending. Exact overrun bounds and accounting remain open; this is not unlimited spend authority.

decisions.title: Clarify and correct wiki conflicts
decisions.rationale: For conflicting wiki information, ask the user for clarification before selecting a version. Correct the wiki, then continue affected work from the corrected record. Do not silently choose or leave disagreement unresolved as the final behavior. Provenance/history and stale-derived-context cleanup remain supporting implementation work.

decisions.title: Proactive simple work; discuss heavy work first
decisions.rationale: Proactively research and perform simpler day-to-day work within existing guardrails. Research and notes can feed coding ideas. Substantial work, such as building a feature, needs a user conversation first. Detailed triggers, topic selection and routing are deferred; this is sufficient direction for this pass.

decisions.title: Add missing capability, then resume task
decisions.rationale: When a user task needs an unsupported feature, inform the user, add the capability where feasible, then resume and complete the original task. Keep the user in the loop. Existing substantial-feature discussion, scoped permissions, dev/PR review and production approval still apply; no bypass or guaranteed feasibility is implied.

decisions.title: Mac performance baseline
decisions.rationale: Initial performance baseline: the user's current MacBook Pro, Apple M2 Pro, 10-core CPU (6 performance + 4 efficiency), 16 GB unified memory, currently macOS 26.7.1. Hardware read locally at the user's request; serial numbers and device identifiers are not recorded. Run efficiently and fluidly on this machine. This is an initial target, not a benchmark-proven minimum; older OS/hardware support remains open.

decisions.title: Phone requests can use authorized Mac
decisions.rationale: Confirmed: requests from the phone may use capabilities on an online, authorized Mac. Scoped permissions remain required; routing and unavailable-device handling remain implementation work.

decisions.title: Preserve both sides of sync conflicts
decisions.rationale: Preserve both versions of conflicting local/cloud edits and ask the user which to keep. Do not silently overwrite either version. Cloud remains authoritative after reconciliation; version tracking and resolution propagation need implementation.

decisions.title: Reviewed approval learning loop
decisions.rationale: Dedicated approval agent evaluates requests, auto-approves within user policy and learns from decisions. April initiates requests through that system. Review repeated routinely approved prompts and promote them to explicit default allowances in operating context/policy. Existing explicit consent boundaries remain until changed by user.

decisions.title: Choose language by requirements
decisions.rationale: No programming-language preference or exclusion. Select implementation based on portability, resource efficiency, fluid interaction and other established requirements; stack choice is an engineering evaluation.

decisions.title: Replace chat/voice/computer-use and Cursor prompting workflows
decisions.rationale: Replace the user's ChatGPT app workflows: text chat, voice conversation and computer use. Later take over much of manual Cursor prompting. Cursor remains an initial integration target; reducing prompting does not necessarily mean replacing the editor. Full parity is a destination, not a v1 promise.

decisions.title: Orchestrate existing tools rather than rebuild them
decisions.rationale: User confirms retaining Cursor as editor, Slack as client and existing browser initially. April orchestrates them, taking over much manual prompting, while providing its own unified voice/chat/artifact surface. This does not select API versus UI adapters.

decisions.title: Cloud-first tasks continue when the Mac disconnects
decisions.rationale: All tasks are cloud-first and most work runs in Cloudflare. All files, including public and private vault contents, have cloud storage as their persistent home and source of truth at all times. The Mac is a lightweight client for voice, visuals and local device integrations; local copies and offline pending changes synchronize with cloud state. Approved cloud tasks, including private-file tasks, continue if the Mac disconnects, within the existing task-scoped grant. Disconnection neither revokes the grant nor expands its scope; private access still expires when the task ends. Operations needing a local integration require that device to be reachable. Encryption-key custody, revocation and enforcement remain implementation work.

decisions.title: Conversations are independent of vaults
decisions.rationale: Conversations are not tied to a particular vault. Vaults organize stored data and access, not conversational sessions. Public-to-April vaults are available to April across conversations without an active-vault switch granting access. Browsing a vault in the UI does not create a new conversation or restrict the conversation to that vault. Private vaults retain explicit task-scoped approval and task-end expiry. This supersedes earlier suggestions that the active vault defines the conversation context; an individual tool operation may still target a specific vault.

decisions.title: Personal, medical and financial vaults; work deferred
decisions.rationale: Initial scope excludes work and any work vault. Start with personal, medical and financial vaults. Work can be reconsidered later. Vaults remain storage/access boundaries, not conversation containers; public-to-April vaults are always available, private data requires task-scoped approval.

decisions.title: One ongoing thread; April manages internal context
decisions.rationale: The user interacts through a single ongoing thread and does not manage separate conversation sessions. April may internally organize, branch and manage task/topic context as needed. Internal context/session boundaries are implementation details, not user-facing vault boundaries. Vaults remain independent storage/access domains. This does not require one ever-growing model prompt or bypass private-data approvals.

decisions.title: Conversation interruption leaves delegated tasks running
decisions.rationale: Spoken interruption stops or redirects the conversation, not delegated tasks. Heavy use of specialist/subagent execution is intended; tasks continue independently of the live conversation and require an explicit user instruction to interrupt/cancel them. Task lifecycle must be separate from voice playback/session lifecycle. Existing failure, permission and safety limits still apply; they are not overridden by conversational independence.

decisions.title: Study internal threading and long-context UX
decisions.rationale: Study Codex's long-conversation and threading experience as a reference for internal context organization. User sees one ongoing thread; heavy subagent use is intended. Specific mechanisms are to be researched, not assumed.

decisions.title: Specialists may delegate further
decisions.rationale: Specialist agents may delegate further to subagents within the original task authority; delegation is not restricted to the main interaction agent. Represent parent/child task relationships and return results through the hierarchy while April remains the single user-facing coordinator. Delegation does not expand private-data access or permissions. Depth/concurrency limits, budget allocation, conflict handling and cancellation propagation remain implementation decisions.

decisions.title: Summary overview and full subagent audit tree
decisions.rationale: Use top-level task summaries for the overview, with the full specialist/subagent parent-child tree available for monitoring and audit. Preserve nested execution lineage, status and evidence; exact UI and audit fields remain design work and private data boundaries still apply.

decisions.title: Pause and resume delegated tasks
decisions.rationale: Provide explicit task pause/resume in addition to cancellation. Voice interruption does not pause tasks. Proposed access is conversational commands and task-summary/tree controls; final placement is not selected. Define safe checkpoints, in-flight actions, child propagation, retained progress and permission revalidation; pausing is not undo.

decisions.title: Coordinator scopes a pause from the user’s reason
decisions.rationale: User supplies a reason for pausing. The coordinator decides which subagents should pause or continue based on that reason, rather than applying a fixed stop-all-children rule. Record the reason and decision for audit. Respect the expressed pause intent; clarify material ambiguity. Safe checkpoints/in-flight handling remain implementation work.

decisions.title: Bring stuck specialist work to the user
decisions.rationale: When a specialist is genuinely stuck, bring the blocker to the user and work through it together. The user sees this as a possible sign that requirements need clarification or the specialist scope is too large. Do not silently substitute specialists, expand scope or run an autonomous repair loop as the default response to being stuck. Preserve task state and resume or rescope after clarification. The definition/detection of a blocker and handling of routine transient errors remain implementation details. Pause reason taxonomy is deferred; user provides a reason when needed.

decisions.title: Auto-send offline requests on reconnect
decisions.rationale: Automatically send requests queued while offline when the client reconnects; no separate queue-review step is required. Sending a queued request is not approval to bypass private access, release or other policy checks. Ordering, deduplication, cancellation of unsent requests and stale-scope handling remain implementation details.

decisions.title: Best-effort automatic voice resumption
decisions.rationale: If connectivity drops during an active voice session, attempt automatic resumption on a best-effort basis. If recovery is not possible, the user can summon April again. Do not revive a session explicitly dismissed during the outage. Preserve visible connection/listening state; do not imply offline voice inference or default audio retention. Recovery deadlines, buffering and failure indicators remain implementation details.

decisions.title: Five-second automatic voice recovery window
decisions.rationale: Bound automatic voice-session recovery to approximately five seconds. If it cannot resume within that attempt window, stop automatic resumption and wait for the user to summon/resume manually. Display recovery/failure state and do not reopen a dismissed session. Exact timer implementation remains engineering work.

decisions.title: Full local copy first; cloud-only on-demand later
decisions.rationale: Initially keep/copy all vault files locally and synchronize everything to the cloud, simplifying the first version. Cloud remains authoritative and private-file agent access stays task scoped. Future direction: fetch only files being viewed or needed, keeping the rest cloud-only. Selective caching/pinning is not required initially. This describes future product behavior, not authorization to copy/upload the user's current files now.

decisions.title: Restorable bin; user reviews every seven days
decisions.rationale: Deleting a vault file removes it from active use and synchronizes deletion while retaining a restorable bin entry. The user's final preference supersedes the earlier automatic seven-day purge idea: prompt the user to review pending deletions every seven days, and let the user clear them at review. Do not permanently purge solely because seven days elapsed. Preserve recoverability until the user explicitly clears the bin. This is a future April product workflow, not a request to create a real reminder/automation now. Bin permissions, private metadata, restores and replica/backup cleanup remain implementation details.

decisions.title: Minimize external disclosure; audit zero retention
decisions.rationale: Process as much data as possible within the user-controlled cloud environment. Send external AI providers, search tools and document-processing services only the minimum necessary content. Heavily audit services and select only those meeting the user's zero-data-retention requirement for the relevant service/endpoint and account configuration. This applies beyond model providers to external tools. No vendor or endpoint is verified or approved by this note; contractual promises, eligibility, exceptions, logging and actual configuration need validation. Private-file access grants do not imply unrestricted downstream disclosure.

decisions.title: Quiet reconnect; optional chime
decisions.rationale: After voice reconnection, do not give a spoken announcement. An optional brief chime may signal recovery; chime choice/settings are not finalized. Preserve the existing approximately five-second automatic recovery window and manual fallback.

decisions.title: Far-future owned inference and private processing
decisions.rationale: Far-future direction: own/control the AI inference layer so private data processing no longer requires sending content to external AI providers. This is not an initial-release requirement and does not establish that a chosen Cloudflare product can host the required models. Preserve a replaceable inference/provider boundary now. Hardware, model quality, operating cost and any remaining external-tool dependencies need later evaluation; the user's goal is to keep data private under their control.

decisions.title: Derived private artifacts stay private
decisions.rationale: Artifacts derived from private material automatically inherit its private classification, including summaries. Do not place them in ordinary/public-to-April memory or expose them through less-restricted artifact views. Existing private-task approval boundaries still apply. Mixed-source classification, explicit declassification and retention/derived-context cleanup remain implementation details; no automatic declassification is selected.

decisions.title: Delete summaries with their private source
decisions.rationale: When a private source file is deleted, its derived summaries are deleted as well and follow the same restorable-bin and user-reviewed permanent-cleanup process. Do not leave the summaries as independently retained private artifacts by default. Maintain source-summary lineage for this behavior. Mixed-source summaries, restore consistency and indexes/embeddings need explicit implementation rules; the user specifically confirmed summaries, not an indiscriminate cascade to every linked document.

decisions.title: Cloudflare-account identity and recovery direction
decisions.rationale: User prefers identity/setup and recovery tied to their Cloudflare account, with Access/OAuth-style facilities to be evaluated rather than a separate recovery-key UX chosen now. Official Cloudflare docs confirm Cloudflare-as-identity-provider support in Access and Managed OAuth for supported non-browser clients; evaluate native-client compatibility, policy, token/device lifecycle and account recovery before selecting the flow. Distinguish application sign-in from OAuth permissions to manage Cloudflare resources and from encryption-key recovery. This does not create/configure accounts, grant credentials or settle key custody.

questions:
Confirmed: approved cloud tasks, including private-file tasks under existing task-scoped access, continue if the Mac disconnects. Next: specify key custody, revocation and device-unavailable handling; all persistent files are cloud-backed.
Engineering evaluation: unified voice overlay and artifact workspace, plugin-ready architecture, low resource use and fluid interactions on the verified M2 Pro / 16 GB Mac.
Private grants: task-end expiry is decided; specify revocation, terminal-state handling, derived-context cleanup, encryption keys and recovery.
Sync: preserve both conflicting edits and ask the user is decided; specify lineage, resolution propagation, deletion and reconnection.
Coding bootstrap: Cloudflare execution, April-only GitHub repositories, dev/PR/user approval flow are decided; validate macOS packaging/native tests and exact release evidence.
Deferred deep dives: plugin contracts/trust, per-integration API versus UI, Codex-inspired computer use and memory systems including Supermemory.
Operational implementation: accurate cost tracking and non-blocking $20 AI nudge, task retry/cancellation, recovery history and permission enforcement.
notes:
Exploration snapshot, not a benchmark or implementation audit. Framework positioning records the discussion as of 31 October 2026. Most alternatives received only high-level review. Preserve rationale when changing status. Export saved edits before reconciling them into the repository.
Direction revision 2: platform-agnostic core, macOS native integration first. Later Windows/Linux support is architectural scope, not simultaneous delivery. Specific GUI, implementation language and process layout remain open.
Voice clarification complete for this pass. Next discussion: Mac experience. Financial and medical information is excluded from ordinary memory; task-scoped access only.
